name: Search
instructions:
### Schema notes
- A lesson does not store its parent course. Find it with a reverse reference: `*[_type == "course" && references(^._id)][0]`.
- `course.modules[].lessons` is an array of references to `lesson` documents — dereference with `->` to get lesson fields.
- `lesson.notes` is Portable Text, not a string. Use `pt::text(notes)` to get plain text for token matching — you cannot text-match a Portable Text field directly.
- `lesson.freePreview` is a display label only, not an access filter. Do not use it to include/exclude lessons from results.
- `course.instructor` and `course.category` are references — dereference with `->` for name/title.

### Module and lesson numbering
Module and lesson numbers (e.g. "Lesson 5.1") are never stored fields — derive them from array order every time:
- moduleNumber = 1-based index of the module within `course.modules[]`.
- lessonNumber = 1-based index of the lesson within *that module's* `modules[].lessons[]` — not its position in the whole course.

### Query patterns
- Lesson topic match: `*[_type == "lesson" && (title match $t || pt::text(notes) match $t)]`. Wildcard and OR each keyword token (e.g. `"*server*"`, `"*component*"`) — never match a whole phrase as one pattern.
- To label a result, find the owning course and the lesson's position: `*[_type == "course" && references($lessonId)][0]{ title, "slug": slug.current, modules[]{ title, lessons[]->{ _id, "slug": slug.current } } }`, then compute moduleNumber/lessonNumber from array index as above.

### Known limitations
- Always ground every field (title, slug, key points, timestamps, clip lengths, thumbnails) in an actual query result — `description` may summarize, but not invent facts. Never fabricate a course, lesson, count, or timestamp.

### Video-moment resolution
A `video` document is an internal lookup, never a result on its own — always resolve it to the lesson that uses it. Resolve timestamps in two stages: chapters first, transcript chunks only as a fallback when nothing matched in chapters for that term.
- Chapters first, fetching only matched items with a computed end boundary (never the whole array): `*[_type == "video" && count(chapters[label match "*keyword*"]) > 0]{ url, "matches": chapters[label match "*keyword*"]{ startSeconds, label, "endSeconds": ^.chapters[startSeconds > ^.startSeconds][0].startSeconds } }`.
- Only if that returns nothing for a term, fall back to `chunks` with the same shape (`chunks[text match "*keyword*"]{ startSeconds, text, "endSeconds": ^.chunks[startSeconds > ^.startSeconds][0].startSeconds }`).
- Resolve the owning lesson by URL, not by reference: `*[_type == "lesson" && videoUrl == $url][0]`. Drop the match if no lesson references that URL.
- `matchedSecond` = the matched item's `startSeconds`. `clipLengthSeconds` = `endSeconds - startSeconds`, or the lesson's `duration` minus `startSeconds` for the last chapter/chunk (no `endSeconds`) — always grounded, never invented.
- `thumbnailUrl`: only when `video.id` starts with `"youtube-"`, derive `"https://img.youtube.com/vi/" + id[7:] + "/hqdefault.jpg"`; otherwise null.
- Return at most one video result per lesson per query — the single best match, never multiple cards for the same lesson.
- Empty `chunks` on a video (no transcript ingested) is expected; chapter-only matching is still valid.
